provenance.title: Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents

facts.statement: Hoplite lets you deploy coding agents in the cloud with a suite of tools that makes it incredibly easy to QA features, mirroring your local setup in the cloud.

Hoplite is designed for developers who want to deploy coding agents that can work on software projects in a real, isolated development environment and automate tasks like editing code, running tests, and opening pull requests.

Hoplite describes itself as a platform for effortless cloud coding agents that can run in isolated sandboxes and handle hundreds of concurrent agents to perform quality assurance and developer automation tasks.

Hoplite built a custom agent harness to gain independence and freedom instead of relying on third-party models like Codex or Claude Code, allowing them to test new features without waiting for external providers like Anthropic and OpenAI to catch up.
facts.value: custom in-house agent harness built instead of third-party models like Codex or Claude Code

facts.statement: Hoplite runs agents in isolated sandboxes in the cloud, each with its own VM, enabling hundreds of concurrent agents to run simultaneously.
Hoplite prepares video recordings of all new feature changes for easy verification without manual walkthroughs, storing these flows in a QA library to be replayed without rerunning agents.
facts.value: QA library with video recordings of feature changes

facts.statement: Users can try Hoplite immediately and freely by signing up with the code ‘HACKERNEWS’ which grants $100 in free credits plus the ability to connect Codex subscription for OpenAI models integration.
Hoplite publishes transparent monthly and yearly pricing plans starting at $99 per seat for Pro and $299 per seat for Scale, including prepaid credits and features tailored for team sizes.
The founders of Hoplite are Bence and Ryan, as stated in the Hacker News launch post.

disqualifiers.statement: The team is named and nothing any of them is stated to have built appears in the evidence, and the company has no public repository.

unknowns: D3 Evidence of pull: unknown — no primary source in this candidate's evidence, scored at uncovered · floor of 6–12

why_this_call.text: Pass — disqualifier D-1 fired, and a cited disqualifier forces a pass whatever the score (60/100, 80% coverage).
The largest shortfall is D1 Founder–market fit & technical depth at 12/25 (band 6–12).
1 of 5 dimensions had no primary source behind them; they are listed under what we could not verify.

what_would_change_my_mind.text: Disqualifier D-1: find a stated prior role for somebody they name, something one of them is stated to have built, or a public repository. It would then no longer hold, and the call would no longer be forced to Pass.
D1 Founder–market fit & technical depth: find a prior employer, role or period stated for somebody the company names. That moves it from 6–12 to 13–19 (+7).
